You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

'Task-45f42459 rule from 4 demos and solved test. Grid has background plus two short border segments of a framing color (examples: vertical segments on opposite left/right edges, or horizontal segments on top/bottom), and isolated marker-color cells between them. Extend each marker in a straight line toward the border segment on its side until just before the border; recolor the marker itself 4 and fill the connecting cells with its original marker color. Then project the marker row/column index within its border segment onto the corresponding opposite border segment: draw a full-width/full-height line of the marker color across the grid from the opposite segment toward the far edge, stopping before a framing-color segment if one is present. Preserve border cells. Alignment is by offset within the two corresponding segments (their start indices), not raw coordinates; e.g. demo with left vertical segment rows 3–14 and right segment rows 17–28 maps r→r+14; test segment rows 2–11 to 14–23 maps r→r+12. Important edge detail: the projected line extends to the grid edge when no opposite border segment occupies that row/column. In the solved test, right edge 9 rows 2–11 and left edge 9 rows 14–23; 7 markers at (r,c)=(2,11),(3,23),(4,17),(6,23),(8,3),(11,15). Each original row was filled with 7 between marker and right-edge 9, marker changed to 4. Projected full 7 rows at r=14,15,16,18,20,23 were filled c=1..26 inclusive; earlier incorrect attempt omitted far-right c=26. One caution: infer projection end from whether a framing segment blocks it; keep background at unblocked far edge? Demos show fill through that edge when no border cell exists there.

Recurrence validation (2026-10-20): new 25x6 test solved on the first submission. Background 6; framing color 3 on right edge rows 0-3 and left edge rows 19-22, with matching offsets 0-3 (left segment is lower in the grid). Marker color 7 at (20,3),(21,4),(22,2), i.e. offsets 1,2,3 within the left-edge segment. For each marker, draw 7 horizontally toward the adjacent left edge through intervening cells and recolor the marker to 4: row20 c1-2=7,c3=4; row21 c1-3=7,c4=4; row22 c1=7,c2=4; preserve left-edge 3s. Copy each active offset (1,2,3) to the corresponding right-edge segment: rows1-3 get 7 across c0-4, preserving framing 3 at c5. Row0 remains unchanged because offset0 has no marker. Accepted. This confirms same-offset mapping between unequal-coordinate opposite edge segments and the rule that projected lines stop before the framing-color edge cell.

Recurrence confirmation (2026-10-20): first-submit solved test, 29x8, background 5, framing color 9 at top row columns 6-7 and bottom row columns 0-1; marker color 2 at (r,c)=(3,0),(12,1). Treat the bottom bar as source side: draw color 2 upward from its cells in active offsets 0 and 1 through the markers, changing markers to 4; the rays cover c0 rows 4-2 and c1 rows 13-2 (all cells to just before top edge). Copy the active offset pattern to the top segment: fill c6 and c7 down through row 28, preserving top 9s; the corresponding far edge has no bar at c6-7, so fill through the edge. Bottom bar 9s are preserved. Output key rows: row3 c0=4; rows4-27 c0=2; row12 c1=4; rows13-27 c1=2; c6,c7=2 for rows1-28. This confirms the rule for top/bottom bars whose spans are horizontally shifted, with aligned offsets rather than identical columns.'
